answer.rationale: Competitor price cut threatens SMB retention through acquisition, not value realization. Memory_73 and exp_73 show promotional pricing drives short-term signup but fails at 30-day retention—repeating this would deepen the churn problem, not solve it. Memory_44 indicates enterprise prospects have stronger fundamentals; memory_57 shows referral incentives work on established customers but do not address immediate churn of price-sensitive SMBs. Instead: activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action, working alongside signup simplification (memory_86, memory_31). The root issue is not price but perceived value gap in early use. Activation messaging re-engages at-risk SMB cohorts by demonstrating product value before renewal conversation, preserving qualified revenue without unsustainable discounting. Standard_experiment scope lets leadership respond today while containing risk; activation messaging has no measured retention harm in the archive and addresses the real lever—engagement velocity, not price matching.
